title: escalate a service issue with relevant diagnostic evidence
input: The incident owner collects affected resource identifiers, timestamps and sanitized reproduction details.
action: AWS Support receives the support case and assists within the account's support entitlement and case scope. Support guidance informs diagnosis; the customer retains responsibility for approved workload changes.
output: The incident owner validates the guidance, applies an approved action and reports the actual result.
check: Confirm application recovery and exclude secrets or unnecessary customer data from the case attachments.

title: modernize a legacy application with reviewed transformation artifacts
input: The application owner selects the supported transformation workload and inventories code and runtime dependencies.
action: Transform analyzes supported legacy workload inputs and produces transformation or modernization artifacts. Proposed changes require engineering review, dependency validation and testing before they replace the production application.
output: The migration team builds the transformed application and validates its business behavior in an isolated target.
check: Compare transaction results, external integrations and performance against the source before an approved cutover.

title: rehost a source server with tested application cutover
input: The migration owner inventories source volumes, operating system and application network dependencies.
action: Application Migration Service replicates supported source server disks and launches test or cutover instances from the replicated data. Target launch settings and replication state determine the resulting EC2 server.
output: The owner tests the application on the isolated target instance before moving client connections.
check: Reconcile replicated state, boot success, dependencies and final writes; keep a rollback plan during cutover.

title: serve a low-latency mobile inference endpoint
input: The developer prepares a supported inference container and carrier-facing connection requirements.
action: Wavelength places supported application infrastructure in telecommunications edge locations. Its configured network path connects eligible mobile clients to the running workload; application code executes the inference.
output: The mobile client receives inference responses from the deployed edge application and handles regional fallback when designed.
check: Measure real carrier-path latency and test unsupported client routes, capacity limits and fallback behavior.

title: coordinate an incident in a restricted communication space
input: The incident team uses approved enterprise identities and assigned communication membership.
action: Wickr provides secure messaging and collaboration under the configured enterprise network and retention controls. Participants exchange incident information through the authorized conversation, not through unrestricted public channels.
output: Responders share sanitized incident updates and supporting files with the assigned team.
check: Verify membership removal, message retention and file access using allowed and excluded test users.

title: publish an internal resolution article for repeated incidents
input: The support lead selects a validated incident resolution and its permitted internal audience.
action: re:Post Private provides a private knowledge and collaboration space for the organization's AWS questions and guidance. Approved contributors curate the resolution article and discussion under the chosen access controls.
output: The operator uses the internal article to diagnose a later incident and validates its applicability before changing resources.
check: Test audience access, remove secrets and review outdated remediation instructions before publication.

title: stream an engineering application to a contractor
input: The contractor signs in through the enterprise assignment for the licensed engineering application.
action: AppStream streams the assigned application from the configured fleet using its approved image and session policy. The application runs on the fleet instance; the contractor interacts through the streaming client.
output: The application accesses only the permitted project files and exports approved results through the configured storage integration.
check: Test fleet availability, application startup, project-file isolation and session termination for a removed assignment.

title: shift traffic during an approved application recovery
input: The recovery operator checks standby readiness and the authorized recovery plan.
action: Application Recovery Controller provides supported recovery coordination capabilities such as routing controls and readiness or zonal recovery features. The selected recovery mechanism changes the intended traffic or zone configuration under its specific safety conditions.
output: The application owner validates the alternate serving path and executes the approved traffic shift using the chosen ARC feature.
check: Test routing safety, dependency readiness and rollback; traffic movement alone does not synchronize application state.

title: record an order through a distributed SQL transaction
input: The order application submits validated order rows and a stable transaction identity.
action: Aurora DSQL stores relational data and executes supported SQL transactions using its distributed architecture. Applications handle concurrency conflicts and retry whole transactions safely rather than assuming every PostgreSQL feature is supported.
output: The application returns the committed order identifier and queries the stored order through an authorized SQL connection.
check: Test conflicting writes, transaction retries and supported SQL features with the actual order schema.

title: serve a variable-demand relational application
input: The application submits authorized SQL queries against the selected Aurora engine and serverless configuration.
action: Aurora Serverless adjusts database capacity according to its configured generation and limits while the engine executes SQL. Capacity changes do not remove connection management, transaction design or supported-engine constraints.
output: The application commits its validated business transaction and reads the resulting rows.
check: Load-test minimum and maximum capacity, idle behavior and connection recovery using the exact serverless version.
